propositions: A failed identity write (add_label or set_entity_property) in dispatch_one.create_one invokes delete_issue, destroying a successfully-created Jira issue to recover from a labeling failure.

The write-ahead binding is recorded keyed-pending before identity writes, so an unhandled rollback leaves a keyed-pending entry pointing to a now-deleted Jira key, stranding the local ticket permanently across retry passes.

The retro-attach recovery path in recover_pending.keyed_branch already exists to deterministically retro-attach labels and properties without search, making the rollback delete redundant and destructive.

Jira field write failures originate from three distinct causes (field not on screen, workflow property jira.permission.createclone.denied, or malformed value) but Jira's error message is misleading in roughly half the cases.
The recovery approach should leave the binding keyed-pending and re-raise the write error unmasked rather than deleting the issue, allowing retro-attach to complete the job on a subsequent pass.
